title: Service-level-aware admission proxy for dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets must simultaneously provide per-customer throughput guarantees and maintain global latency SLOs under bursty load. Current fleet routing admits requests first-come-first-serve and relies on coarse autoscaling; this leads to noisy-neighbor amplification and occasional latency SLO violations during correlated spikes.

Goal: Build a deployable admission-proxy layer that enforces service-level-aware pacing and overload policies at the fleet ingress. The proxy should: (1) enforce per-tenant throughput contracts (guarantees + best-effort), (2) maintain global headroom for latency-critical traffic, (3) integrate with autoscaler signals to reduce manual tuning, and (4) expose observability and knobs for rollout and on-call operators.
acceptance_criteria: Admission proxy accepts and enforces per-tenant throughput guarantees defined as guaranteed_rps and burst_rps in fleet config
Under a 3x synthetic spike, 95th-percentile latency for guaranteed tenants stays within target SLO (configurable; default 150ms) while best-effort tenants are degraded predictably
Autoscaler receives headroom and queue-length signals and can scale the fleet within defined cooldowns such that backlog is reduced by >= 50% within one scaling step in test harness
Proxy emits metrics for per-tenant admitted_rps, rejected_rps, queue_depth, average_wait_ms, shedding_count and routing_fallbacks; dashboards created and linked
Fallback behaviors (route to cheaper model, degrade to token-limited responses, or fail-fast) are configurable per-tenant and exercised in integration tests
design_summary:
We propose a lightweight admission proxy colocated with fleet ingress that implements a two-tier shaping model: 1) Reservation buckets: each tenant with a committed throughput gets a token-bucket reservation (guaranteed path) sized by guaranteed_rps * headroom_window. Reservations have soft borrowing rules to allow short temporary bursts with accounting. 2) Shared best-effort pool: capacity not reserved is placed in a global best-effort bucket used by non-guaranteed tenants.

The proxy also maintains age-ordered per-tenant queues with admission priorities derived from SLA (guaranteed > gold > silver > bronze). Queue admission uses aging to prevent starvation and an admission controller that consults a predictive autoscaling estimator: if predicted capacity will arrive before max_wait_ms for an item, the proxy will retain the item; otherwise it applies shedding policy.

Shedding policies are pluggable: 1) degrade-to-smaller-model (rewrite routing target), 2) partial-response tokenization (limit tokens to N), 3) reroute-to-burst-pool (non-SLA burst capacity), 4) immediate-reject with SLA-aware HTTP status. The proxy exposes a control API for operators to adjust reserved_capacity_pct, max_queue_ms, and predictive thresholds.

Trade-offs: We choose per-tenant token buckets vs. strict per-tenant queues to reduce memory pressure on large fleets; soft borrowing increases fairness but requires accounting to avoid overcommit. Predictive autoscaling reduces unnecessary shedding but adds complexity and dependency on estimator quality. The initial rollout will keep estimator in advisory mode (no automatic scaling) until confidence thresholds are met.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Deploy proxy in front of a single small dedicated fleet with advisory-mode estimator and observe for 2 weeks
Phase 1 (limited): Enable enforcement for bronze/gold tiers only; preserve guaranteed tenants in reservation mode; run chaos simulations with synthetic spikes
Phase 2 (scale): Expand to all dedicated fleets with automated estimator hooks enabled for autoscaler (read-only initially), dashboards and alerts onboarded
Phase 3 (full): Enable predictive autoscaling-driven admission adjustments and fully automated fallback policies for non-critical tenants
updates: 2026-03-02 - Ticket created by Asha; initial problem statement and goals added.
2026-03-04 - Spike: built a proxy prototype in Go that enforces per-tenant token buckets; initial perf shows ~2% added P50 latency at 1k rps/fleet in canary env (Diego).
2026-03-06 - Design review with Platform and SRE: agreed to keep estimator advisory for first two phases; added requirement for observability and circuit-breaker fail-open behavior (SRE feedback).

2026-03-08 - Implemented per-tenant accounting and a global best-effort pool; ran internal load test with synthetic 5x burst. Observed guaranteed tenants maintained p95 under 140ms but bronze tenants saw >70% rejection; tuned soft-borrow window. PR 4721 opened.
2026-03-10 - UX session with PM (Lena Cho): added control knobs in Console (reserved_capacity_pct and max_queue_ms). Documented defaults and per-tenant overrides.
2026-03-12 - Integration tests: added an end-to-end test that validates degrade-to-smaller-model fallback. Next: run chaos tests and hook autoscaler readouts.
